title: Effective stress: Terzaghi's principle of grains, water and total stress
examples: What is effective stress in soil?
How do you calculate effective stress below the water table?

layers.label: Dry sand 2 m
layers.ask: What is total stress in soil?

explain.say: Karl Terzaghi, the father of soil mechanics, said soil strength depends not on the total weight pressing down but on how hard the grains push on each other. He called that effective stress. On the board, two metres of dry sand sit over three metres of wet sand. Let us find the stresses at point A, five metres down.

draw.text: Effective stress: Terzaghi's principle of grains, water and total stress

layers.label: Dry sand 2 m
layers.ask: What is total stress in soil?

explain.say: First the total stress, the weight of everything above A. Two metres of dry sand at eighteen kilonewtons per cubic metre gives thirty six kilopascals. Three metres of saturated sand at twenty adds sixty more. So the total is ninety six kilopascals.

layers.label: Dry sand 2 m
layers.ask: What is total stress in soil?

explain.say: Below the water table the pores are full of water under pressure, which pushes the grains apart. At A, three metres below the water table, the pore water pressure is nine point eight one times three, about twenty nine point four kilopascals. Do the grains feel this as extra squeeze, or as lift?

layers.label: Dry sand 2 m
layers.ask: What is total stress in soil?

explain.say: As lift! The effective stress is total minus pore pressure: ninety six minus twenty nine point four, about sixty six point six kilopascals. See the three lines: total on top, water at the bottom, effective in between. It is effective stress that controls strength and settlement.

curves.label: Total stress
curves.ask: What is total stress in soil?

explain.say: Now the wow. If water flows upward hard enough, pore pressure rises until effective stress falls to zero. The grains stop pressing on each other and sand behaves like a liquid: quicksand, or liquefaction in an earthquake, as in Niigata, Japan, in nineteen sixty four. Superb! Challenge: if the water table rose to the surface, what would happen to the effective stress at A?

draw.name: x-why
draw.question: Why can sand suddenly act like a liquid?
draw.answer: With no grain contact, sand flows like a liquid

faq.a: Effective stress is the part of the total stress carried by the soil grains pressing on each other: total stress minus pore water pressure. At point A it is 96 minus 29.4, about 66.6 kilopascals.

faq.q: What is total stress in soil?
faq.a: Total stress at a depth is the weight of everything above it per unit area: soil, water and any surface load. Here 2 metres at 18 plus 3 metres at 20 gives 96 kilopascals.
asks: How do you calculate total stress?

faq.a: It is the pressure of the water in the soil pores. Below a still water table it equals the unit weight of water, about 9.81 kilonewtons per cubic metre, times the depth below the water table.
asks: How do you calculate pore pressure?

faq.q: Why does effective stress control soil strength?
faq.a: Soil strength comes from friction between grains, and friction depends on how hard they press together. Water pressure pushes them apart, so only the effective stress creates friction.

When pore water pressure rises until it equals the total stress, effective stress drops to zero. The grains lose contact and the sand flows like a liquid, from upward seepage or from earthquake shaking.

facts: Karl Terzaghi set out the effective stress principle in the 1920s; his book Erdbaumechanik appeared in 1925.
In the 1964 Niigata earthquake in Japan, soil liquefaction tipped over apartment buildings.

quiz.say: At a point the total stress is 150 kilopascals and the pore water pressure is 50. What is the effective stress?
quiz.show: Total stress is 150 kPa and pore water pressure 50 kPa. Effective stress?
quiz.why: Effective stress = total − pore pressure = 150 − 50 = 100 kilopascals.

wrong.1: Pore pressure is subtracted, not added.
wrong.2: That divides the two stresses; effective stress is a difference.

quiz.say: If the water table rises, the effective stress at a fixed depth…
quiz.show: If the water table rises, the effective stress at a fixed depth…
quiz.why: Pore pressure rises more than the total stress, so the grains are pushed apart.

wrong.0: Wetter soil weighs a bit more, but the extra water pressure outweighs that.
wrong.2: Pore pressure changes with the water table, so effective stress must change.
